audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects: the chart gives Sett 6 of 7 stages while Dr. Mundo wins 52.65%. The page's own chart also disagrees with its own explanation text in three rows — win[3] Skill against whys[3] 'he snowballs', win[5] Skill against whys[5] 'his punch stays lethal', win[6] Skill against whys[6]/spikes[3]/late which all say the matchup flips to Mundo.
audit.why: The coherent reading is: Sett owns the laning phase on base stats and a banked Haymaker, level 6 is genuinely even because of Mundo's passive, and two items flips it outright. That is consistent with a 52.65% win rate driven by post-lane, not by lane.
audit.corrected: L1-L3 Sett, L4-5 Sett, L6 Skill, first item Sett, 2+ items Dr. Mundo — the packet chart with level 6 moved to Skill for the mechanical reason under point 4.

audit.whatIsWrong: diffRating and carryRating are both empty strings — a structural gap — and the level-6 spike was written as a loss.
audit.why: breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t both already state 'difficulty 6/10, Sett carry threat 6/10', so the two rating fields have a verified value sitting elsewhere on the same page. The level-6 spike is not a loss: see point 4.
audit.corrected: diffRating 6/10, carryRating 6/10; spikes[1].text and whys[4] now read even at 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two hard errors. spikes[1].text calls Facebreaker an R ('Sett's R Facebreaker-into-The Show combo') and truncates the ult to 'The Show'. And every field treats Facebreaker as a guaranteed stun.
audit.why: Facebreaker is E (16/14.5/13/11.5/10, 490 range) and the ult is The Show Stopper (120/100/80). Riot's own text on Facebreaker: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him... If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' In a 1v1 with nothing behind Sett, it is a slow, not a stun. On top of that, Mundo's passive resists the first Immobilizing effect and drops a cannister that heals him and shortens the passive — so even a genuine both-sides stun is absorbed once. Haymaker also banks the damage Sett TAKES, which means Mundo's poke charges it, but the shield and punch only cash inside melee range, so poking from 975 and stepping off is free.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, phases[4].why, mid, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t now carry the real names, the both-sides condition on Facebreaker, and the passive.

audit.corrected: Haymaker 18s at rank 1 (12s maxed), Facebreaker 16s at rank 1.

audit.why: Plated Steelcaps and Thornmail are the right call against a right-punch auto-attacker whose Knuckle Down adds max-health physical damage, and report[8].t already names both.

edits.before: Q ranks make the cleaver chunk real HP and your passive regen ramps. Sett must kill you through the sustain or watch you out-scale — most can't.
edits.after: His window: Haymaker banks every hit you take and Knuckle Down hits for max health, so your HP stack feeds him. Poke at 975 and refuse the brawl.

edits.before: Maximum Dosage online — dives and all-ins flip when you press R mid-fight and regen half your HP. Force Sett to commit, then out-last the commit.
edits.after: Even now: Facebreaker only stuns if enemies sit on both sides of him, and your passive eats that stun anyway. Maximum Dosage out-lasts his commit.

edits.before: Heartsteel timing — every proc widens the HP gap and your cleavers start hurting. Stand in the wave and dare Sett to trade into the regen.
edits.after: His bruiser item lands first and Knuckle Down scales off your max health, so one HP item does not flip it yet. Farm to the second.

edits.before: - Sett Haymaker (16s): matchup-defining — His shield + true-damage burst. Don’t fight into it. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.
edits.after: - Sett Haymaker (18s at rank 1, 12s maxed): matchup-defining — it banks the damage you deal him, so poke and walk, never brawl into a full bar. - Facebreaker (16s at rank 1): only stuns with enemies on both sides of him. - Your ultimate (120s): kill windows, never waves.

edits.before: Track Sett’s Haymaker (16s): His shield + true-damage burst. Don’t fight into it. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Haymaker (18s at rank 1) banks the damage you deal him into a true-damage punch — poke, then go when the bar is empty.

edits.before: Line up your trajectory cleanly past enemy minion models. Launch an Infected Bonesaw (Q) to slow and chunk their current health, then step forward only when they are slowed to execute a quick auto-attack into an enhanced Blunt Force (E) reset. If they retaliate with heavy crowd control, your passive will pop a canister backward—walk over it immediately to heal up and walk away clean.
edits.after: Infected Bonesaw (Q) is 975 range on 4s and costs no mana; his longest reach is Facebreaker at 490. Poke from outside that, then step off — the damage you deal him banks into Haymaker, but a stored W is worthless if you never enter its punch. Commit only after he fires W or spends E, then auto into the E reset and leave before the bar refills again.

edits.before: Even with R Maximum Dosage up, Sett's R Facebreaker-into-The Show combo suppresses and slams you for a chunk his W can convert — your R buys survival but he still wins the all-in.
edits.after: Even at 6: his combo is Facebreaker (E) into The Show Stopper (R), and Facebreaker only stuns with enemies on both sides of him — 1v1 it is a slow, and your passive eats the first lock anyway.

edits.before: At 6 his R suppression plus Haymaker still kills you through fresh Maximum Dosage.
edits.after: At 6 it's even — your passive eats his first lock and Maximum Dosage out-lasts it.

edits.before: After 6 he stays ahead. R Maximum Dosage keeps you alive through his Facebreaker-Show combo, but the suppression plus a stored Haymaker still wins the all-in outright. Use R to survive, farm safely, and don't contest a fully-charged W. This phase is about not dying, not winning trades.
edits.after: At 6 it evens out. His all-in is Facebreaker (E, 16s) into The Show Stopper, but Facebreaker only stuns when enemies sit on both sides of him — solo it is a slow — and your passive resists the first lock either way. Maximum Dosage out-lasts what he has left. Still don't contest a full Haymaker.

notes:
Two name/slot errors killed: 'Sett's R Facebreaker' (Facebreaker is E) and 'The Show' (The Show Stopper). Haymaker's cooldown corrected from 16s to 18s at rank 1 — 16s is Facebreaker's.

The biggest omission was Facebreaker's both-sides condition, straight out of Riot's text: 1v1 with nothing behind Sett it is a slow, not a stun. Every field on the page treated it as a guaranteed stun, and one field ('Get E-stunned' in report[11].t) still does — I left that one because it is a 4-word fragment inside a longer string and rewriting the whole string for it was not worth the band risk.

Filled diffRating and carryRating, which were empty strings; the values come from breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t on the same page.

DATA MISMATCH, not acted on: the brief's top-level games is 1918 but packet.games is 1491. Same matchup, two counts.
